newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian ruling party tells partner to clean up act.
newsitem.headline: Belgian ruling party tells partner to clean up act.

text.p: Belgium's ruling Christian Democratic party CVP told its main government coalition partner, the francophone socialist party PS, on Monday to get its act together to remain credible.
"We think the situation is serious," CVP chairman Marc Van Peel told Belgian VTM television after the party's executive committee met.
"From now on we will follow up from day to day what is happening at the PS," Van Peel said.
The PS has acknowledged it had contacts with two firms at the centre of allegations about illegal party financing.
The so-called Dassault and Agusta scandals centre on claims the French and Italian companies of the same names paid kickbacks to Belgian parties in the late 1980s to win lucrative defence contracts.
Both firms have consistently denied any wrongdoing.
Belgium did not restrict corporate funding of political parties until 1989 and only banned it completely in 1993.
The CVP said in a statement it wanted to update the government programme ahead of next month's 1997 budget review and set priorities for the final two years of its legislature.

"The most important criteria is whether this government can carry on with its work...we hope that the government can go on, but this assumes that the PS will continue to put things right internally," he said.
"It remains to be seen whether the PS will be able to be a firm coalition partner," he said. -- Bert Lauwers, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6815, Fax +32 2 230 7710
